Completion must reference the created product and occur only after successful atomic input conversion. Provide reusable visual metadata for work-in-progress and prepared-food stacks: component food, mode cold-combined, ingredient resource IDs and proportions, quantity, condition, state, progress and a derived ingredient palette. Show hand preparation only during real work; show the completed meal only when it exists. Do not depict a bowl, utensils, fire, steam or cooked texture without corresponding real objects and processes. Interrupted, failed or incomplete work remains visibly unfinished; eating visuals and effects require a real eat event. Visual labels and presentation confer no safety, nutrition, experience or mastery.

Before implementation, reconcile the retained registry search results with full implementation contracts in the existing development handoff; if an equivalent parameterized operation exists, reuse its code and record that dependency rather than implement a duplicate. Reuse inventory transfer, food properties, decay, work scheduling and eat contracts. Inputs must be real, accessible, actor-owned edible ingredients with applicable known safety evidence; nontoxicity alone does not establish that an otherwise inedible material is ready to eat. Cold preparation requires usable hands and the ability to handle the selected food, but no vessel, water, fuel or fabricated tool. No washing, cutting, heating, sterilization, detoxification, preservation or digestibility improvement is implied. Other modes require their actual implemented mechanisms and physical prerequisites, not an automatic unlock. Reference Ivo's berry knowledge record berry, nutrition 8 and toxicity 0, and owned stack item-3-ivo-30, resource berry, quantityTenths 30, quantity 3. Validate its live quantity, accessibility and condition at execution. Preparing all three units would produce one three-unit berry meal with nominal total nutrition 24 and zero recorded berry toxicity, subject to existing food-condition rules. The observed root sources, including commons-root-5-0 and start-1-roots, are not owned ingredients: reaching and gathering them must occur separately under navigate and gather, with actual stock and energy costs. Do not expose unobserved stock. Accept positive tenths-unit quantities. Work required equals selected ingredient quantity in simulation time units at one unit per round, with energy cost 1 per ingredient unit worked; a three-unit batch therefore takes three active rounds and 3 energy, in addition to any travel, gathering, learning or eventual eating costs. Validate sufficient energy for each work increment; do not overdraw. At start atomically transfer selected quantities into a real work-in-progress container, preserving ownership, mass, provenance, nutrition, toxicity and decay history. It is a bookkeeping/product container, not a granted physical utensil. Record recipe, inputs, paid work, elapsed progress and position. Progress requires actual actor participation; no unattended preparation or review-time progress. Spoiled or lost inputs cannot support completion. Cold prepared food has no ongoing fuel or equipment maintenance, but ordinary carrying, storage, decay and exposure rules continue.
